tagline: Global leader in advanced textiles and materials processing for paper, industrial, and aerospace markets
hero_kpi_rationale: The Machine Clothing segment is the company's primary revenue driver, representing approximately 60% of its consolidated sales. Its performance is a key indicator of the company's overall financial health.

kpis.name: Machine Clothing Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the design and manufacture of fabrics and belts for the paper industry and other industrial applications.
kpis.description: The Machine Clothing segment recorded revenue of $708.1 million in 2025, down 5.6% from 2024 ($749.9 million), impacted by reduced demand for PMC products in Asia and strategic consolidation of facilities in Europe.
kpis.signal: Decline in revenue from the core segment, affected by weaker demand in Asia and strategic divestitures in Europe.

kpis.name: Albany Engineered Composites Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the manufacture of high-performance composite components and assemblies for aerospace and other industries.
kpis.description: The Albany Engineered Composites segment recorded revenue of $474.7 million in 2025, down 1.2% from 2024 ($480.7 million), primarily due to production challenges and increased inflationary costs on certain programs, notably the CH-53K.
kpis.signal: Slight revenue decline driven by operational challenges and cost adjustments on long-term programs.

kpis.name: Total Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Consolidated revenue of the company, including all its business segments.
kpis.description: Total net revenue reached $1,182.8 million in 2025, down 3.9% from 2024 ($1,230.6 million), primarily due to the performance of the Machine Clothing segment, which was impacted by reduced demand in Asia.
kpis.signal: Overall revenue decline, reflecting trends in both segments and operational challenges in the AEC segment.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Consolidated gross margin reached 20.6% in 2025, down from 32.6% in 2024, primarily due to estimated charges of $165.8 million for adjustments to estimated profitability on AEC programs, notably the CH-53K.
kpis.signal: Significant gross margin contraction due to restructuring charges and cost adjustments on long-term AEC programs.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting operating expenses, including selling, general, administrative, and restructuring costs.
kpis.description: Consolidated operating margin in 2025 was nearly zero (estimated at approximately -0.4% after considering $280.0 million in operating expenses and $243.9 million in gross profit), affected by operational challenges in the AEC segment.
kpis.signal: Negligible to nearly zero operating margin, impacted by restructuring charges and profitability adjustments on AEC programs.

kpis.name: R&D Investments (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Research and development expenses (Technical and research expenses) reached $48.0 million in 2025, representing 4.1% of net revenue, up from 3.7% in 2024, primarily due to increased activity from the New Business Ventures group.
kpis.signal: Sustained R&D investment with focus on new composite technologies and commercial ventures.

kpis.name: General and Administrative Expenses (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Selling, general, and administrative expenses expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: SG&A expenses reached $218.3 million in 2025, representing 18.5% of net revenue, up from 17.1% in 2024, reflecting higher personnel costs, professional fees, and investments in information systems.
kpis.signal: Increase in SG&A expenses due to higher personnel costs, professional fees, and global IT system investments.

kpis.name: Restructuring Charges
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to operational restructuring, including facility closures and site consolidations.
kpis.description: Net restructuring charges amounted to $13.7 million in 2025, slightly higher than $13.4 million in 2024, reflecting ongoing rationalization initiatives, including consolidation in Europe, closure of the South Korea facility, and the strategic review of the Amelia Earhart Drive facility in Utah.
kpis.signal: Ongoing restructuring expenses related to the rationalization of the MC segment's operational footprint and the closure of AEC's assembly structures division.

kpis.short: Impact des ajustements sur programmes AEC
kpis.name: Cumulative Impact of Estimated Profitability Adjustments (AEC)
kpis.explanation: Cumulative charge due to adjustments in cost and profitability estimates for certain long-term AEC segment programs.
kpis.description: In 2025, the AEC segment recorded a cumulative charge of $165.8 million due to adjustments in profitability estimates on certain long-term programs. This amount includes $155.9 million adjustment related to the CH-53K program, of which $147.3 million was recognized in the third quarter, including a $98.0 million loss reserve for higher-than-expected labor costs and elevated material inputs due to inflation.
kpis.signal: Significant financial impact of $165.8 million resulting from operational challenges and cost inflation on fixed-price contract programs in the AEC segment.

kpis.short: Part des revenus liés aux contrats gouvernementaux US (AEC)
kpis.name: Share of Revenue from US Government Contracts (AEC)
kpis.explanation: Percentage of AEC segment revenue derived from contracts or programs linked to the US government, including defense programs.
kpis.description: In 2025, approximately 35% of the AEC segment's net revenue was linked to US government contracts or programs, notably the CH-53K, F-35, and JASSM programs, highlighting its strategic importance but also its customer concentration risk.
kpis.signal: High dependence of the AEC segment on US defense contracts, creating customer concentration risk.

kpis.short: Part des revenus liés au client SAFRAN (AEC)
kpis.name: Share of Revenue from Customer SAFRAN (Consolidated)
kpis.explanation: Percentage of the company's consolidated revenue derived from customer SAFRAN through the AEC segment and the joint venture Albany Safran Composites (ASC).
kpis.description: In 2025, sales to the SAFRAN group, via Albany Safran Composites (ASC), represented approximately 15% of the company's consolidated revenue (estimated $175-180 million), primarily for CFM LEAP aircraft engine components and GE9X fan cases.
kpis.signal: Significant concentration of consolidated revenue on a key aerospace customer, representing the largest customer.

risks.title: Industry Consolidation and Competitive Pressure
risks.score_rationale: Significant consolidation in the paper industry has reduced global consumption of paper machine clothing in certain markets. The shift toward digital media has reduced demand for newsprint and printing paper, affecting MC segment revenues. The company faces ongoing pressure to provide more favorable commercial terms.

risks.title: Operational Challenges and Inflationary Costs (AEC)
risks.score_rationale: The AEC segment recorded a cumulative charge of $165.8 million in 2025 due to cost adjustments on long-term programs, notably $155.9 million for the CH-53K. Inflation in labor and material costs, combined with workforce and production challenges, significantly impacted the profitability of fixed-price contracts.

risks.title: Dependence on US Government Contracts
risks.score_rationale: Approximately 35% of AEC segment revenue depends on US government contracts, notably defense programs (CH-53K, F-35, JASSM). Changes in DoD policy, budget decisions, or program suspensions could significantly impact revenue and profitability.

risks.title: Restructuring and Execution Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company has announced the strategic review and potential sale of the Amelia Earhart Drive facility in Utah, including exit from the structures assembly business and CH-53K work. The MC segment restructuring is a multi-year program involving integration of Heimbach operations and includes site closures in South Korea, Italy, France, and the UK.

risks.title: Customer Concentration and Supply Chain
risks.score_rationale: SAFRAN represents approximately 15% of consolidated revenue through Albany Safran Composites. The AEC segment relies on global supply chains that have experienced disruptions. Fixed-price contracts offer little flexibility in the event of rising material or labor costs.

ai_positioning.summary: The company AIN does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report. The information provided focuses on financial aspects, business segments, and company operations, with no reference to AI.
